Theme

tune noun

a melody

also melody, tunes, in tune, out of tune, hum a tune

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.106: flēbilibus modīs concinere (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 7.2: saltāre ad tībīcinis modōs (Lewis & Short)

modus, modī m.

noun, second declension

a tune, a melody (usually plural, modī)

The measured run of the notes: melody, rhythm and time together. Mostly plural: flēbilēs modī, a sad tune. The everyday sense of modus is a measure, a limit, or a way (see manner).

Other words

  • cantus, cantūs m. — a song or tune, sung or played

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical

    The singing or playing itself; see song.

  • absonus, absona, absonum — out of tune

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.41: vōx absona atque absurda (Lewis & Short)

    Of a voice or instrument off the note; also, more generally, out of keeping with something.

Examples

  • Quōs modōs canis? Nōn agnōscō.

    What’s that tune you’re singing? I don’t know it.composed

See also song, sing, musical, the same old song, musical instrument.
